To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) pulse-triggered flipflops are the most SEU-SET-tolerant pipeline latches, and (2) pulse-triggered and edge-triggered flip-flop structures are the most MBU-tolerant pipeline flip-flops.
the pulse-triggered flip-flip is the best choice in terms of delay, energy consumption and complexity.

the pulse-triggered flip flop is a good choice for SEU and SET tolerant designs, that the level-sensitive latch is the best choice for SEU tolerant designs, that differential designs have the best energy performance, and that the master-slave flip flop has the best complexity performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of pipeline latches and edge-triggered flip-flop structures that exhibit high levels of radiation immunity, while maintaining low power consumption and high performance.
the design of SEU and MBU tolerant pipeline latches and pipeline flip-flops.
the development of radiation-hardened-by-design (RHBD) structures that can be utilized in pipeline latches and pipeline flip-flops.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differential pulse-triggered flip flop (PTFF) is the most promising design for a pipeline memory cell in the 90 nm CMO technology.

the pulse-triggered master-slav flip-flop is the most effective pipeline latch and flip-flop for SEU and SET mitigation at the 90nm technology node, and that this structure is capable of achieving SEU and SET immunity with minimal energy and performance penalties.
pulse-triggered flipflops are the most effective in terms of performance and complexity, while level-sensitive latches are the most energy efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed hardened-by-design techniques can be applied to any latch or flip-flop design to improve its SEU, SET, and MBU tolerance.
SEU and SET tolerant designs are feasible, and that the performance, energy consumption and complexity of such designs are acceptable.
SEU and SET tolerant pipeline memory cells can be constructed with a modest increase in area and power consumption over non-tolerant cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the 90 nm node and beyond, the energy and performance costs of SEU and SEU/SET tolerance are not prohibitive.
a number of SEU and MBU-tolerant designs can be implemented at low cost and with low area overhead.

a number of hardened-by-design SEU and SET tolerant pipeline latches and master-slave flip flops are available to designers, and that these hardened-by-design techniques can be used in conjunction to provide MBU tolerance.
